==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈkɪl/|[ˈkʰɪɫ]|a=RP,US,CA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-kill.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-kill.wav|a=Southern England}} *** {{IPA|en|[ˈkʰɪʊ̯]|[ˈkɪɤ̯]|a=l-vocalization}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪl|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=to put to death}} From {{inh|en|enm|killen}}, {{m|enm|kyllen}}, {{m|enm|cullen|cüllen|t=to strike, beat, cut}}, of obscure origin. Cognate with {{cog|sco|kele}}, {{m|sco||keil|t=to kill}}. * Perhaps from unattested {{inh|en|ang|*cyllan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kwulljan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kwuljaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʷelH-|t=to throw, hit, hurt by throwing}}. * Or, possibly a variant of {{inh|en|ang|cwellan|t=to kill, murder, execute}} (see {{l|en|quell}}). * Or, from {{der|en|non|kolla|t=to hit on the head, harm}}, related to {{cog|no|kylla|t=to poll}}, {{cog|dum|kollen|t=to knock down}}, {{cog|is|kollur|t=top, head}}; see also {{l|en|coll}}, {{l|en|cole}}). Compare also {{cog|stq|källe|t=to hurt}}, {{cog|dum|kellen|t=to kill, hurt}}, {{cog|gml|kellen}}, {{m|gml|killen|t=to ache strongly, cause one great pain}} (whence {{cog|nds-de|kellen}}, {{m|nds-de|killen|t=to hurt, injure, torment, vex}}), {{cog|gmh|kellen|t=to torment; torture}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|en|k1ll||filter-avoidance spelling}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To put to [[death]]; to [[extinguish]] the [[life]] of. #: {{ux|en|Smoking '''kills''' more people each year than alcohol and hard drugs combined.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|act=IV|scene=vi|page=304|passage=A Troope of Horſe with Felt: Ile put't in proofe, / And when I haue ſtolne vpon theſe Son in Lawes, / Then '''kill''', '''kill''', '''kill''', '''kill''', '''kill''', '''kill'''.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|III|ii|page=12|passage={{smallcaps|Stephano}}: {{w|Caliban|Monſter}}, I will '''kill''' this man : his daughter and I will be King and Queene, ſave our Graces : and ''Trinculo'' and thy ſelfe ſhall be Vice-royes : {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author=Justin O. Schmidt|title=The Sting of the Wild|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|isbn=978-1-4214-1928-2|page=102 |passage=Fire ants circumvented the problem of an ineffective sting by having an unusual and highly effective venom that when daubed or sprayed on other ants penetrates their waxy protective integumental barrier and '''kills''' or disables them.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Holly Yan|title=5 years after the Parkland school massacre claimed 17 lives, here’s what has changed (and what hasn’t)|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/14/us/parkland-school-shooting-5-year-anniversary|date=2023-02-14|passage=As the country reckons with how to prevent more children from being '''killed''' at school, the legacies of the Parkland victims live on.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008131840/https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/14/us/parkland-school-shooting-5-year-anniversary|archivedate=8 October 2025}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal='To reduce their environmental impact, why not simply regulate the weight of cars?', Le Monde|date=2024-09-16|passage=After all, improving road safety has become a widely endorsed cause because nobody wants to '''kill''', or be '''killed''', in a road accident.|author=Stéphane Foucart }} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Sharon Otterman|title=Trump Threatens Columbia With Millions in Cuts Over Antisemitism Claims|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/04/nyregion/trump-columbia-antisemitism.html|date=2025-03-04|passage=In announcing the review, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the new health secretary, said in a statement that “antisemitism — like racism — is a spiritual and moral malady that sickens societies and '''kills''' people with lethalities comparable to history’s most deadly plagues.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312213556/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/04/nyregion/trump-columbia-antisemitism.html|archivedate=2025-03-12}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To render [[inoperative]]; to [[shut off]], [[extinguish]], or [[put out]]. #: {{ux|en|He '''killed''' the engine and turned off the headlights, but remained in the car, waiting.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|year_published=1959|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Moonraker (novel)|Moonraker}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter=Cards With A Stranger|page=47|passage=He reached for his cheroot and gave it a final draw, then '''killed''' it in the ashtray.}} #* {{quote-av|en|year=1978|author=w:John Farris|title=[[w:The Fury (1978 film)|The Fury]] |passage=''Peter'': Ask Childers if it was worth his arm.
''Policeman'': What did you do to his arm, Peter?
''Peter'': I '''killed''' it, with a machine gun.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To [[stop]], [[cease]]{{,}} or render [[void]]; to [[terminate]]. #: {{ux|en|The editor decided to '''kill''' the story.}} #: {{ux|en|The news that a hurricane had destroyed our beach house '''killed''' our plans to sell it.}} #: {{ux|en|My computer wouldn't respond until I '''killed''' some of the running processes.}} # {{senseid|en|amaze}} {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively|hyperbole}} To [[amaze]], [[exceed]], [[stun]]{{,}} or otherwise [[incapacitate]]. #: {{ux|en|That night, she was dressed to '''kill'''.}} #: {{ux|en|That joke always '''kills''' me.}} #* {{RQ:Salinger Catcher|page=23|passage=He told us we ought to think of Jesus as our buddy and all. He said ''he'' talked to Jesus all the time. Even when he was driving his car. That '''killed''' me.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive|figuratively|hyperbole}} To cause great [[pain]], [[discomfort]]{{,}} or [[distress]] to; to [[hurt]]. #: {{ux|en|These tight shoes are '''killing''' my feet.}} #: {{ux|en|You don't ever want to get rabies. The doctor will have to give you multiple shots and they really '''kill'''.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2008|month=October|author=Davy Rothbart|title=How I caught up with dad|journal=w:Men's Health|volume=23|issue=8|issn=1054-4836|page={{gbooks|VMgDAAAAMBAJ|110|killing}}|passage={{smallcaps|two laps into our first walk, my dad}} needed to sit down. His back and legs were '''killing''' him. "You'll be okay," I assured him. "You just need to shake off the rust."
I gave him a couple of Advil and, after a few minutes, urged him back onto the track.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively}} To [[produce]] [[feeling]]s of [[dissatisfaction]] or [[revulsion]] in. #: {{ux|en|It '''kills''' me to throw out three whole turkeys, but I can't get anyone to take them and they've already started to go bad.}} #: {{ux|en|It '''kills''' me to learn how many poor people are practically starving in this country while rich moguls spend such outrageous amounts on useless luxuries.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[use up]] or to [[waste]]. #: {{ux|en|I'm just doing this to '''kill''' time.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Jonathan Franzen|title=The Corrections |passage=Except for the shirt, which he’d worn, and the check, which he’d cashed, and the bottle of port, which he’d '''killed''' in bed on Christmas night, the gifts from his family were still on the floor of his bedroom.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively|informal}} To [[overpower]], [[overwhelm]]{{,}} or [[defeat]]. #: {{ux|en|Look at the amount of destruction to the enemy base. We pretty much '''killed''' their ability to retaliate.}} #: {{ux|en|The team had absolutely '''killed''' their traditional rivals, and the local sports bars were raucous with celebrations.}} # Most place names with '''''kill''''' were derived entirely in Dutch, but many have been subsequently {{lg|calqued}} into English or [[anglicize]]d by {{lg|folk etymology}}; for example, {{m|en|Motherkill}} and {{m|en|Murderkill}} both likely derive from {{m+|nl||*Modderkil|Mud Creek}} (better preserved in {{m|en|Mudder Kill}} and {{m|en|Muddy Kill}}), originally having nothing to do with mothership or murder. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}}{{tlb|en|Northeast US|chiefly|New York}} # {{topics|en|Landforms|Water}}{{lb|en|archaic|or|regional|largely {{lg|fossilized}} in place names}} A [[creek]] or [[stream]]; {{lb|en|more loosely}} any [[watercourse]], such as a [[channel]] or [[arm]] of the sea. #: {{ux|en|The channel beyond Staten Island, which connects Newark Bay with Bergen Neck is the '''Kill''' van Kull, or the '''[[Kills]]'''.}} ## {{lb|en|preceded by ''[[the]]''}} In particular, a waterway with a name ending in '''''kill''''', such as the Beaverkill or the East Kill. ##: {{ux|en|We're gonna go flyfishing over in the '''kill'''.}} {{rfquote|en}} =====Usage notes===== * No longer seems to be {{lg|productive}}, whether for deriving new {{lg|compound}}s or discussing [[waterway]]s not already called '''''Kill'''''. Almost exclusively used in proper names based on waterways, mainly [[tributary|tributaries]] of the [[Hudson]] and [[Delaware]] rivers and a few [[saltwater]] channels of [[New York City]]. The region in which they are found comprises southeastern [[New York State]] and adjacent parts of other states, i.e. former [[New Netherland]], itself roughly coinciding with [[Lenapehoking]] plus [[Mohican]] land, the area having been settled and (re)named by Dutch colonists in the 17th century prior to English acquisition. Compare the geographic term {{m|en|clove|id=valley}} for a similar case; {{m|en||hook}} (from {{m|nl|hoek}}) and {{m|en|-burg}} are also found as a second element of Dutch-origin [[toponym]]s.
